1  ORDER

This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 02.02.2013 passed by MACT, Dewas in Claim Case No.128/2011 seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the permanent disability suffered by the appellant/claimant, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,55,200/- along with interest.

The break up of the compensation amount is as under:
Permanent disability -Rs.70,200/- (i.e. Rs.3000x12x15% (PD)x13)

Medical expenses -Rs.25,000/-
 Future treatment -Rs.5,000/-
 Loss of income -Rs.10,000/-
 Pain and suffering -Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of prospects of life -Rs.15,000/-
Misc. expenses during treatment-Rs.15,000/-

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding adequate amount of compensation as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side,
hence prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel fort he Insurance Company has argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.

5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, in the considered opinion of this Court, the Tribunal has not awarded just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

Considering the evidence came on record, in the considered opinion of this Court, the income of the injured was assessed on the lower side by the Tribunal at Rs.3000/- p.m which deserves to be increased to Rs.3,600/- p.m.
As per the medical certificate came on record the appellant has suffered 46% permanent physical impairment in his upper/lower extermity.
The percentage of the permanent disability suffered by the appellant/injured is also wrongly calculated at 15% which should be assessed at least 20%.
The Tribunal has also not awarded any amount under the head of future prospects.

Considering the overall facts and totality of the circumstances, in the considered Ramchandra vs Dilshad And 2 Ors. on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197049994/
2 opinion of this Court

, the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced as under:
Permanent disability -Rs.1,40,400/- (Rs.3600 25% FPx20% PDx12x13) Medical Bills -Rs.25,000/-
 Future treatment -Rs.5,000/-
 Loss of income -Rs.10,000/-
 Pain & suffering -Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of prospects of life -Rs.15,000/-
Misc. expenses during treatment-Rs.15,000/-
-----------------
TOTAL Rs.2,25,400/-
==========
6.
Thus, the appellant is entitled to the total compensation of Rs.2,25,400/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.1,55,200/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.70,200/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
7. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.70,200/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
